verdict: Klarna passed $1B in revenue for the fourth straight quarter and its transaction margin jumped 32% to $371M, but share-based pay and other costs still left a $65M net loss.

segments.name: Transaction and service revenue
segments.note: Fees Klarna earns when shoppers check out with buy now, pay later and other payment products — $36.1B of purchases flowed through in the quarter.

segments.name: Gains on consumer receivables, net
segments.note: Gains from selling consumer loans onward to other buyers through Klarna's forward-flow programs — about $7.7B of loans were sold in the quarter.

segments.name: Interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on the loans Klarna keeps on its own books, mainly its Fair Financing instalment loans.

flow.costPlain: What each purchase costs Klarna to run: $255M to process and service payments, $201M set aside for credit losses, and $182M to fund the loans.

opex.name: Technology and product development
opex.note: Engineers and designers building Klarna's app, card and checkout products.

opex.name: Sales and marketing
opex.note: Winning merchants and shoppers, including the Fiserv partnership and new U.S. retailers.

opex.name: Customer service and operations
opex.note: Support for 122 million active consumers and 1.35 million merchants.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company: finance, legal, risk and offices.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of software and other long-lived assets, plus small impairments.

otherDetail: Other income (expense) was a $3M gain — immaterial next to the operating loss.
follow100Note: Klarna's transaction costs — processing, credit-loss provisions and funding — eat $63.23 of every $100 before its own running costs, and the quarter ended in a loss, so the 'kept as profit' row is negative. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: It keeps much more from each purchase than a year ago
takeaways.text: Transaction margin — what Klarna keeps after paying to process, fund and cover losses on each purchase — rose 32% to $371M, or 36.8% of revenue, up 5.7 points. Fair Financing, its highest-earning product per dollar of volume, was also its fastest growing, up 61%.

takeaways.title: Subscriptions are becoming a real business
takeaways.text: Subscription revenue rose more than 500% to $43M in the quarter — $178M a year at September's run rate — as paying Klarna Card subscribers tripled to 2.6 million. Card volume more than doubled to $4.5B, and card users shop with Klarna about three times as often.

takeaways.title: Still loss-making on the official books
takeaways.text: The operating loss was $53M and the net loss $65M, both $30M better than a year ago. Share-based payments jumped 38% to $54M on the timing of the annual compensation cycle; strip those and depreciation out and adjusted operating income was +$21M, up $35M year over year.

oneTimers: Share-based payments were $54M, up 38% year over year, on the timing of Klarna's annual compensation cycle — the company says they should return to pre-Q3 levels. They are the main reason adjusted operating income (+$21M) is $74M above the reported operating loss ($(53)M), along with $22M of depreciation and amortization, partly offset by a $2M restructuring gain.
Gains on consumer receivables of $53M are new this quarter (nil a year ago) — they come from Klarna's forward-flow loan-sale programs, which sold about $7.7B of loans in the quarter.
footerNote: Klarna reports under IFRS. 'Transaction margin dollars' — revenue minus processing, credit-loss and funding costs — is its gross-profit line; the $21M adjusted operating income excludes $54M of share-based payments and $22M of depreciation and amortization.
pngFooterNote: IFRS reporter; transaction margin is its gross-profit line.
